title: Wine Glass Emoji 🍷 Meaning: Unwinding, Dates and Class
description: 🍷 means wine, unwinding after a long day, date nights and a touch of sophistication. Explore how the wine glass emoji is used in texts and captions.
summary: The 🍷 wine glass emoji means wine, most often red, and the moods that go with it: relaxing in the evening, dinner, date night and girls' night. It can suggest sophistication or self-care, and it is also used to joke about coping with stress.
meaning: Where a beer says the workday is done, a glass of red says the evening has begun. 🍷 is used for pouring a glass at home, dinner out, tastings and vineyard trips. It often stands for a mood more than a beverage: a slow night, a bath, a show, a deep conversation. “🍷 and a movie” describes a plan in which the wine is half the appeal.

It carries overtones of taste and romance. Wine goes with candlelit dinners and anniversaries, so the emoji can warm up an invitation: “dinner and 🍷?” is more date-like than suggesting beers. It also signals refinement, sincerely or tongue in cheek. People add it to posts about cheese boards, Italian vacations and “classy” behavior, sometimes ironically, as when drinking boxed wine on the couch.

A large share of its use is coping humor. “It's wine o'clock,” “mommy needs her 🍷” and “this meeting could have been a 🍷” treat wine as the reward for surviving the day. The “wine mom” persona made this a recognizable genre, and it has drawn some criticism for making light of heavy drinking. Among friends, 🍷 remains the standard emoji for a night of talking with a bottle open.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: Evening plans and decompression are the main uses. “Rough day, come over 🍷” is an invitation to vent. Friends organizing a night in pair it with cheese or a film. A single glass sent late in the day often just reports that the sender has clocked off and is relaxing.

contexts.label: From a crush
contexts.body: Wine suggests intimacy. An offer of “a glass of 🍷 at my place” is a clear romantic move, and even a restaurant suggestion with the emoji leans toward a real date. It is grown-up flirting, not explicit, but the implication of a lingering evening is there.

contexts.label: In captions
contexts.body: Travel and food posts use it for wine regions, tasting flights, pasta dinners and sunsets. Lifestyle accounts use it for self-care evenings. It marks holidays that involve a festive table, such as Thanksgiving and Christmas dinner, and appears in Passover and Shabbat posts, where wine has ritual meaning.

contexts.label: Among friends
contexts.body: Girls' night, book club and “wine night” are nearly synonymous with this emoji. A row of glasses in a group chat means everyone is in. It is frequently paired with 💅 or 😂 for an evening of gossip, and with 📚 by book clubs that admit the wine matters most.

confusedWith.difference: 🥂 depicts two champagne flutes toasting and is for celebrations and congratulations. 🍷 is one glass of still wine and is about relaxing, dining or romance.
🍸 is a martini-style glass, suggesting bars, nightlife and dressing up. Wine is quieter and associated with meals and evenings at home.
🍇 represents the fruit and winemaking. It suits vineyard and harvest content and is alcohol-free in tone, while 🍷 is the drink in hand.

avoid: Avoid joking about needing wine to cope with someone who has shared concerns about their drinking.
Don't send it to colleagues in a way that could read as a date invitation unless that is your intent.
Leave it out when writing to people who abstain for health, recovery or religious reasons.
design: A stemmed glass about half full of red wine is the standard on every major platform. The glass is clear with a round bowl, and the wine ranges from bright ruby to deep burgundy. No vendor shows white wine or rosé, so people use the same emoji for all varieties.

faqs.q: What does 🍷 mean from a guy?
faqs.a: Often that he is proposing a date-style evening, such as dinner or drinks at home, with romantic intent. It can also simply mean he is relaxing with a glass. Compared with a beer emoji, it suggests more effort and intimacy.

faqs.q: What does 🍷 mean from a girl?
faqs.a: She may be unwinding, inviting you to a wine night, or suggesting a date. With friends it usually means a night of talking. In a flirtatious chat it signals openness to a cozy evening together.

faqs.q: Is there a white wine emoji?
faqs.a: No. The only wine glass emoji contains red wine on all platforms. For white or sparkling wine, people use 🍷 anyway, or choose 🥂 or 🍾 when the occasion is celebratory.
It is a joking phrase for the time of day when it feels acceptable to pour a glass, usually early evening. People post it with 🍷 to announce they are done with responsibilities for the day.

faqs.q: When was the wine glass emoji added?
faqs.a: It dates to the original emoji set standardized in 2010 and has kept essentially the same design, a stemmed glass of red wine, on every platform since then.
